articles.summary: This week's girls Athlete of the Week nominees are from Dallas, South Salem, North Salem, Regis, Kennedy and McNary. Vote!
articles.body:
Who should be Maps Credit Union girls Athlete of the Week?

Every week, the Statesman Journal collects some of the top high school athletic performances to nominate for Athlete of the Week. You're invited to nominate athletes each week by submitting the athlete's name, school, sport and stats relevant to the performance being nominated. Submit nominees to LBartlett@statesmanjournal.com.

The window for nominations is Saturday morning to Friday evening.

Without further ado, here are the nominees for girls Athlete of the Week, brought to you by Maps Credit Union.

Anadeliz Lopez Flores, North Salem soccer

Ariana Salazar Tapia, Kennedy cross-country

Information about each nominee is below. Vote for who you think should win at statesmanjournal.com/sports. The poll closes at 9 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 29.

Anderson, a sophomore, ran a personal-best 19-minute, 25.7-second 5,000-meter race for seventh place at the Happy Hustle race Oct. 21 in Corvallis.

Kartye, a junior, had 11 kills and a block Oct. 20 in the Saxons' four-set win over Sprague to secure a Central Valley Conference championship.

Koehnke, a sophomore, ran a personal-best 11:36.9 3,000-meter race for seventh place at the Valiant Invitational Oct. 20 at Valley Catholic.

Lopez Flores, a senior, scored twice Oct. 22 in the Vikings' 4-1 win over McKay.

Salazar Tapia, a junior, ran a 22:38.5 5,000-meter race for 10th place at The Bigfoot Classic Oct. 21 in Tillamook.

Schlag, a sophomore, scored a goal Oct. 22 in the Celtics' 2-0 win over West Salem to claim the Central Valley Conference title.

See photos as South Salem girls volleyball beats Sprague to win league

Landon Bartlett covers high school sports and Oregon State for the Statesman Journal. He can be reached at LBartlett@statesmanjournal.com or on X, TikTok or Instagram @bartlelo.

articles.title: Updated SEC football conference standings following Week 8 upsets
articles.summary: The SEC's Week 8 slate produced a number of notable results. Here is how those results impacted the conference standings entering Week 9.
articles.body:
Week 8 in the SEC produced yet another eventful Saturday of action for the conference overall.

With four SEC teams on a bye, the conference was home to one of college football's most anticipated matchups of the week, a battle of ranked teams as Texas hosted Ole Miss on Saturday night. In addition to that top 25 matchup, four other ranked SEC teams were in action against unranked conference foes, with two going on the road to play in challenging environments.

Many of those same games went on to produce notable results as well, headlined by an upset taking place as South Carolina stunned Tennessee on the final play with a game-winning field goal. Alabama also avoided a near upset at home to Texas A&M with a big fourth quarter, while Texas defeated Ole Miss in a classic.

As a result, there is now one team solely atop the SEC standings based on winning percentage coming out of Week 8, while a number of teams are very close behind with either one-or-two conference losses.

Here is a look at the updated SEC regular season standings entering Week 9.

Updated SEC football conference standings after Week 8

T-4. Florida, Ole Miss, LSU, Tennessee (3-2)

T-11. Mississippi State, Auburn, South Carolina (2-3)

articles.title: Sixers' Jaylen Brown responds to former Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown responds to former Boston Celtics teammate Jayson Tatum.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- So, one now has to wonder what qualifies as beef and what falls under the lamb chops category?

The situation surrounding Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown and Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum took another turn recently as Brown left a blue hat emoji--internet slang "cap", which means somebody's lying--on a video of Tatum recounting his feelings of the trade . That then set off alarms in both Boston and Philadelphia as one wonders what's next for the duo as everybody moves forward.

Tatum then had a lengthy response, which can be seen fully transcribed here , as he claims there is now beef between himself and Brown. Tatum expressed frustration that due to Brown no longer being on the Celtics, they can no longer have conversations and such.

After a win over the Milwaukee Bucks , Brown gave a very interesting response.

"I didn't see the full thing, but I saw that he said there's no beef and I think he's right," Brown said. "There's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He got a great PR team. There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. You know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times."

Hmm, a great PR team. Lamb chops. Gravy. What exactly is Brown trying to say?

"Just, that's what it is," Brown said. "No beef. It should never, ever be that. It's just basketball. We're both blessed. It might be a little lamb chop. We'll be all right."

Tatum added he wants to have a conversation with Brown.

"We both got so much stuff in front of us," the 2024 finals MVP said of any convos. "So, at the end of the day, we both … He's got to do what he's got to do for his team. I got to do what I do for my team. Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef, but it be a little lamb chop."

So, lamb chops. Not fully beef. Brown is a member of the Sixers. Tatum is leading the Celtics. Obviously, there's something going on between the two of them, but it remains to be seen how everybody will handle this as time moves on.

"Look, like I said, there's no beef," Brown finished. "The PR and all that type stuff, it is what it is, but I think we just both focused on what's in front of us."

The Sixers and the Celtics will match up for the first time on Nov. 10 at the Xfinity Mobile Arena.

articles.title: What channel is Colts v. Vikings game on today? Time, schedule, prediction
articles.summary: What TV channel is the Colts vs. Vikings Week 7 game on today? Here is how you can watch and stream.
articles.body:
Up next for the Indianapolis Colts is a road matchup with the Minnesota Vikings .

The Colts will enter this game at 2-4 and in desperate need of a win. Minnesota, meanwhile, is 5-0 and coming off their bye week.

Here is how you can watch this week's game.

Best of Colts' Week 4 win in London over Commanders

What TV channel is Colts vs. Vikings on?

How to watch Colts vs. Vikings Week 7 game

Announcers for Colts v. Vikings Week 7 game

On the call for this game will be Ian Eagle, with Ross Tucker providing the analysis. On the sidelines will be Evan Washburn.

There are seemingly countless reasons to pick against the Colts in this game after how the season and the last week have unfolded. However, ESPN's Seth Walder feels differently. His bold prediction for the week is that the Colts find a way to win.

"The Colts will win. It doesn't make sense: The Vikings are undefeated, and the Colts literally just fired their general manager," Walder wrote. "But football doesn't always make sense. And I can't get over the fact that the Vikings have recorded a minus-0.09 EPA per play with QB Kyler Murray on the field this season. One of these games, Flores' defense won't be able to secure a win on its own."
